subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Anthology poems (Relationships, Conflict, Time and place, or Belonging)
Language, form and structure in the anthology poems
Themes and meanings across the collections

questions.q: How many named collections make up the Pearson Edexcel GCSE English Literature poetry anthology?
questions.explain: The anthology is divided into four collections: Relationships, Conflict, Time and place, and Belonging.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four Edexcel anthology collections?
questions.explain: Relationships is one of the four collections, alongside Conflict, Time and place, and Belonging.

questions.q: Robert Browning's 'My Last Duchess' appears in which anthology collection?
questions.explain: 'My Last Duchess', a dramatic monologue about a jealous Duke, is set in the Relationships collection.

questions.q: Who wrote 'The Charge of the Light Brigade', found in the Conflict collection?
questions.explain: Tennyson wrote 'The Charge of the Light Brigade' about the doomed cavalry charge during the Crimean War.

questions.q: Which poet wrote the Conflict-collection poem 'War Photographer'?
questions.explain: Carol Ann Duffy wrote 'War Photographer', which explores a photographer developing images of distant suffering.

questions.q: Which of these poems belongs to the Conflict collection?
questions.explain: Wilfred Owen's 'Exposure', about soldiers suffering in the trenches, is part of the Conflict collection.

questions.q: What is the specification code for Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9-1) English Literature?
questions.explain: 1ET0 is the Edexcel GCSE English Literature code; 9ET0 is the A-level and 8702/J352 belong to other boards.

questions.q: In the anthology poetry section of the exam, how many anthology poems are printed on the paper for the student?
questions.explain: One named poem is printed, and the student compares it with a second poem of their choice from the same collection.

questions.q: When comparing two anthology poems, what should the response focus on most?
options: Similarities and differences in ideas and the methods the poets use
Which poem is longer on the page
Only the biographies of the two poets
Reciting each poem word for word
questions.explain: A strong comparison examines how both poets present ideas and the techniques they use to do so.

questions.q: In Carol Ann Duffy's 'Valentine', why does the speaker offer an onion as a symbol of love?
options: It represents love's complex, layered and sometimes painful truth
It shows love should always be sweet and simple
It proves the speaker cannot afford a real gift
It suggests love is unimportant to the speaker
questions.explain: The onion's layers, tears and lasting scent make it an honest emblem of love's difficult, enduring reality.

questions.q: The repeated line 'rode the six hundred' in 'The Charge of the Light Brigade' mainly serves to emphasise the soldiers':
options: Cowardice in the face of danger
questions.explain: The insistent refrain honours the cavalry's courage as they obey orders and ride knowingly towards death.

questions.q: A dramatic monologue, such as 'My Last Duchess', is best defined as a poem in which:
options: A single speaker unwittingly reveals their character to a silent listener
Two speakers argue back and forth in dialogue
The poet directly states their own personal feelings
A chorus comments on the main action
questions.explain: The Duke's own words expose his controlling, jealous nature to a listener who never speaks.

questions.q: What kind of conflict does Gillian Clarke chiefly explore in 'Catrin'?
options: The loving yet tense bond between a mother and her child
A battle between two rival armies
A clash between science and religion
questions.explain: 'Catrin' presents domestic, emotional conflict as a mother and daughter struggle between love and separation.

questions.q: In 'Sonnet 43' ('How do I love thee?'), Elizabeth Barrett Browning uses the sonnet form to:
options: Express the depth and constancy of the speaker's love
Mock the idea of romantic devotion
Describe a violent quarrel between lovers
Argue that love always fades with time
questions.explain: The sonnet, a traditional love form, lets the speaker catalogue and intensify her boundless devotion.

questions.q: In 'Exposure', Wilfred Owen presents the soldiers' greatest enemy as:
options: The freezing weather and deadly waiting rather than the opposing army
A single enemy sniper hidden nearby
questions.explain: Owen makes the merciless cold and stagnant inaction, not the enemy soldiers, the real killers.

questions.q: In 'Half-caste', John Agard uses non-standard English and irony mainly to:
options: Challenge prejudice and defend his mixed heritage
Show that dialect is inferior to standard English
questions.explain: Agard's playful Creole voice and irony expose the absurdity of the insulting term 'half-caste'.

questions.q: A student studying the Relationships collection is given 'The Manhunt' as the printed poem. For the comparison they should choose a second poem:
options: That is an unseen contemporary poem
From a different exam board's anthology
questions.explain: The comparison must be with another poem drawn from the same collection the student has studied.

questions.q: Which opening for a comparison paragraph shows the strongest technique?
options: Make a comparative point about both poems' ideas, then analyse a method from each
Describe everything in the first poem, then everything in the second
Retell the story of each poem in order
List only the rhyme schemes of both poems
questions.explain: Integrated comparison of ideas and methods addresses the assessment objectives far better than describing poems separately.

questions.q: A student notices that both 'Poppies' and 'War Photographer' show conflict's lasting effect on individuals. This is an example of comparing poems through:
options: Their shared theme and the poets' differing methods
The colour of the printed page
The order they appear in the anthology
questions.explain: Linking a common theme and then contrasting the poets' techniques is exactly how effective comparison works.

questions.q: A student is given a printed Conflict poem to compare. Which would be a valid second poem to choose?
questions.explain: 'A Poison Tree' is in the Conflict collection, so it can be compared; the others belong to different collections.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE English Literature (1ET0) specification; Poetry Anthology Collection
